idea-plugin.name: Maven Dependency Overrides
idea-plugin.description:
Detects Maven <dependencyManagement> version overrides that have become stale because an imported BOM chain has caught up — the typical case is a version manually pinned ahead of a CVE fix that Spring Boot's own dependency management later provides at or above the pinned version.

What it does

  • Compares each pinned version against what the BOM chain actually manages it at, and warns directly in the editor, as a weak warning on the <version> tag, on the two cases worth acting on: a pin the BOM has exactly caught up to (now redundant) and a pin sitting below the BOM's own version (holding the dependency back). A pin still raising the version above the BOM stays silent — it's still doing its job. Quick fixes remove the override once it's no longer needed, or suppress the warning with a shared marker comment.
  • Provides a Maven Overrides tool window that lists every detected override across all pom.xml files in the project in one table, with a Status column, add / edit / remove actions, and click-to-navigate to the exact <version> tag.
  • Shows the full parent-chain path from the module down to the BOM that actually manages the version (e.g. spring-boot-starter-parent → spring-boot-dependencies → jackson-bom:2.21.2) — not just the bare BOM name, which is often something the developer never wrote themselves.
  • From the tool window's context menu, Show BOM Chain opens the complete chain for a row: every BOM consulted in precedence order, the one whose version actually applies, the ones that don't manage the dependency, and the ones that couldn't be read from the local repository. Where an unreadable BOM outranks the one that would otherwise win, the chain says the answer isn't known rather than naming a winner it can't vouch for — which is exactly what an inconclusive verdict is telling you. Analyze Dependencies hands the artifact off to IntelliJ's own Maven Dependency Analyzer to see what pulls it in.
  • Adding an override is guided: the tool window's + Add action offers separate Group ID and Artifact ID fields, each backed by what the target module's BOM chain actually manages, with type-to-filter and a browsable dropdown. The version field prefills from what's already managed, alongside a live note on what the version you type would mean — redundant, above the BOM, below it, or not comparable.

How it decides

Detection is local-only: it reads whatever BOM POMs are already in your local Maven repository. When a BOM in the chain can't be resolved there, the override is reported as inconclusive instead of confirmed, and no "safe to remove" quick fix is offered — a wrong "safe to remove" recommendation could silently reintroduce a patched CVE.

Requirements

IntelliJ IDEA (Community or Ultimate) with the bundled Maven support enabled. Any BOMs involved in the check must be present in the local Maven repository (i.e. the project has been imported at least once).
